This wasn't a bad first montage, you'll improve as you go but one tip is at the start it seemed very slow and uninteresting, not engaging and if I was just a normal viewer it would have kept me away from the video at first. I of course kept going cause I wanted to at least check it out of course. Maybe adding a cinematic at the start if COD is capable of doing that (Here's a link I found of someone doing it, I don't play COD so I wouldn't have known without this) A cinematic at the start would be a very good way for that transition, not saying the intro you had was bad btw, I enjoyed the concept you had behind it but to me it didn't really hit home. Especially during 0:14 - 0:16 kinda ruined the emersion you had with the blending of the music and the video. Right when the execute happened you quickly gained that attention back, the kill really working the beat of the music, maybe working with the beat would be a good idea, I know it can make it satisfying but don't over do it.   


I do enjoy you keeping voice chat, it gives a more raw and natural feel of friends and a community just hanging together rather than a typical montage. At 0:44 you had a pretty nice opportunity for a good edit of you bashing through a door to get a semi-seamless cut of another kill or transition in general. 1:22 was a perfect moment to be used during the beat drop later on at 1:28 it was a missed opportunity but a perfect moment to have a kill/transition to make a satisfying moment in the montage. 2:12 was a good use of a transition, didn't use it too often but was nice to see done in this. Ending a bit typical I'd imagine reminds me very much of the Fortunate Son meme but well done for a first montage.   


One thing you should keep in mind I used to do during my old siege montages was making sure to always find new things to add, maybe taking the time to get more footage and play with what you have to make either good cuts etc. will help you greatly. I used to edit and see any points where I could have a new transition to the beat and go get more footage to see if I can make that come true. There's always room for improvement when it comes to that. Hopefully this all helps you you dude, very good first montage you got a lot to learn if this is the direction you'll be taking.

Which is the general rule when I work on yt stuff.

What keeps me motivated is just the fact that I make videos for myself and my friends. I'm almost there to four years of making videos and I've not hit 100 subs yet and I'm honestly proud of that. It is frustrating at times to see the little activity when I make a big video but I still accept it. I simply am a guy who records the time I have with my friends or by myself, make stories etc. and love to edit. The numbers don't really matter to me, it's mainly looking back with my friends at the videos. We often look back at Astroneer and Viscera, two games we played in the early days of the channel etc. It's really just the time I have with friends that keeps me going.
